name: rescue-effect
title: The rescue effect: immigration lowers extinction (Brown & Kodric-Brown 1977)
question:
In the canonical MacArthur-Wilson model the immigration curve I(S)=(P-S)c and
the extinction curve E(S)=S*e are independent. Brown & Kodric-Brown (1977;
citekey brown1977turnover) argued they are not: a population fed by immigrant
propagules is less likely to blink out, so immigration also *lowers*
extinction — the rescue effect. How does coupling the two curves this way
raise equilibrium richness and reduce turnover compared to the
independent-curves baseline?
hypothesis:
If the same colonization pressure c that fills empty niches also rescues
present species (each present species rescued per tick with probability c, its
extinction probability then cut to e*(1-rescue_strength)), the effective
per-species extinction rate becomes e_eff = e*(1 - c*rescue_strength). The
extinction curve is pulled down, so the rate crossing slides right: equilibrium
richness rises to S* = P*c/(c + e*(1-c*rescue_strength)) and the equilibrium
event flux S*·e_eff — the turnover — falls. With rescue_strength=0 the model
reduces exactly to the independent-curves MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium.
objective:
Over a rescue-strength gradient (9 islands, r = 0.0 .. 0.8, matched area and
isolation) on an 8-seed ensemble, measure (a) the ensemble-mean equilibrium
richness S at each rescue strength against the analytic S*(r), and (b) the
equilibrium turnover (gross colonization+extinction events per generation) at
each rescue strength; report the matched no-rescue (r=0) vs with-rescue (r=0.8)
comparison, and verify that at r=0 the simulated S* matches the analytic
MacArthur-Wilson S* = P*c/(c+e). Render the richness-rising, turnover-falling,
and coupled rate-crossing figures.
description:
This study extends the independent-curves MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium
(mw-equilibrium-reproduction) with the rescue effect of Brown & Kodric-Brown
(1977), who found that immigration to boulder-field "islands" propped up
resident populations and flattened the expected species-area/isolation
relationships. The RescueEffectProcess keeps every rule of
MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess but lets the incoming colonization pressure
also rescue present species from extinction, coupling the two rate curves. A
single run sweeps rescue strength at fixed area and isolation, isolating the
coupling as the only varying quantity.

expected_behavior.name: rescue-raises-richness
expected_behavior.en:
Coupling immigration into extinction raises the ensemble-mean equilibrium
richness: the with-rescue island (r=0.8) holds clearly more species than the
no-rescue island (r=0) at matched area and isolation.
expected_behavior.rationale:
Rescue cuts the effective extinction rate to e*(1-c*rescue_strength), pulling
the extinction curve down so the rate crossing S* = P*c/(c+e_eff) slides to a
higher richness.

expected_behavior.name: rescue-lowers-turnover
expected_behavior.en:
The rescue effect damps turnover: the equilibrium gross-event rate (gross
colonization+extinction events per generation) is lower with rescue than
without.
expected_behavior.rationale:
At equilibrium the event flux is S*·e_eff; rescue lowers e_eff faster than it
raises S*, so fewer species are lost (and, by balance, fewer gained) per
generation — the turnover falls even as richness rises.

behavior_tests.name: rescue-raises-richness
behavior_tests.description: With-rescue equilibrium richness must exceed no-rescue by > 2 species.

provenance.note:
Measured S = 37.26 at r=0.8 vs 30.10 at r=0 (margin +7.16 species;
9-island rescue gradient, 8-seed ensemble, 400 generations, tail 25%,
c=e=0.5, P=60). The simulated gradient tracks the analytic
S*(r)=P*c/(c+e(1-c*r)) across all levels (30.00 -> 37.50). 2.0 is a
conservative floor for "clearly more species".

behavior_tests.name: rescue-lowers-turnover
behavior_tests.description: No-rescue turnover must exceed with-rescue turnover by > 2 events/gen.

provenance.note:
Measured equilibrium turnover 30.02 events/gen at r=0 vs 22.56 at r=0.8
(drop 7.45 events/gen; turnover ratio 0.752), same ensemble. Turnover
falls monotonically along the rescue gradient. 2.0 is a conservative
floor for a clear reduction.

behavior_tests.name: r0-matches-baseline
behavior_tests.description:
At rescue_strength=0 the process must reduce to the independent-curves
MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium: simulated S must match analytic S*=P*c/(c+e).

provenance.note:
Measured S_obs(r=0) = 30.10 vs analytic MacArthur-Wilson S* = 30.00
(|err| = 0.10 species), confirming exact reduction to the baseline when
rescue is off. 1.5 is the ensemble-noise tolerance.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
With the rescue effect shown to raise equilibrium richness and damp turnover
(and to collapse onto the baseline when rescue is off), the coupled-curve
extension is validated and available for the species-area/isolation
flattening that Brown & Kodric-Brown (1977) attributed to rescue.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Rescue gradient: richness rising + turnover falling (9 islands, 8-seed ensemble)

conclusion:
Coupling the two MacArthur-Wilson curves reproduces Brown & Kodric-Brown's
(1977) rescue effect. As rescue strength rises from 0 to 0.8, the ensemble-mean
equilibrium richness climbs from 30.1 to 37.3 species (+7.2) while the
equilibrium turnover falls from 30.0 to 22.6 gross events per generation
(ratio 0.75) — richness up, turnover down, exactly as predicted. The simulated
gradient sits on the analytic S*(r) = P*c/(c + e(1 - c*r)) at every level, and
at r=0 it collapses onto the independent-curves MacArthur-Wilson S* = 30.0
(|err| 0.10), confirming the model is a faithful extension of the baseline
rather than a different model. Immigration lowering extinction is enough to
raise equilibrium diversity and stabilize species identity.

r0-matches-baseline.detail: at rescue=0, S=30.10 vs analytic M-W S*=30.00 (|err|=0.10).

findings.statement: Coupling the curves via the rescue effect (immigration lowering extinction) raises equilibrium richness (30->37) and damps turnover (30->23 events/gen), reducing exactly to the independent-curves baseline at rescue=0 (Brown & Kodric-Brown 1977).
